comment: Rebench roster: every config that earned a 'strong' verdict AND is still in service (ornith-iq2m + unraid-laguna were dropped 2026-09-23: weakest configs on the coherent rebench, 86% and 82%) in the earlier swe40 / LCB-60 campaigns, expressed as a bench target. Local targets are mutually exclusive (one GPU workload at a time) and are switched with llama-switch, which stops the whole fleet, verifies VRAM drained, then starts the one asked for. expect_model guards the stale-server trap: an endpoint already answering with a DIFFERENT model is switched instead of trusted. Unraid targets are endpoint-only and were unreachable on 2026-09-22 (ssh reset, :18006 silent).

targets.notes: Daily Qwen3.8-27B Q5_K_M, MTP n=2, 128K ctx, q8_0 KV. Prior: LCB-60 48/60 (best local), swe40 107/112 @27.5 t/s. Thinking LOW is its measured sweet spot.
Same weights/regime as -low, thinking disabled per request. Prior LCB-60 33/59: the policy costs this model ~15 points. Kept in the roster to measure that gap on the new suite, not to recommend it.

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 176B AD384 IQ4_XS, -ngl 99 with expert FFN on CPU, 131072 ctx. Thinking is pinned server-side to reasoning_effort=low, so thinking=null inherits it. Prior: LCB-60 54/60 (quality king) @16.9 t/s, swe40 105/112.
Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B MTPv2-23G-ICE, dual-GPU layer split, 128K ctx. Prior: swe40 110/112 39/40 @~61 t/s (best swe40 of any config). LCB-60 never measured — this campaign fills that gap.
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-IQ3_XXS on the Unraid box (container llm-qwen38-flash, -ncmoe 48 experts on DDR4, 262K ctx). Prior: LCB-60 47/60 @15.6 t/s. Unreachable 2026-09-22 — verify before queueing.

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next AD384, reasoning_effort=medium sent PER-REQUEST via chat_template_kwargs (verified 2026-09-23: request overrides the unit's low pin; template supports low/medium/xhigh only, no off). Effort sweep variant of flashnext-ad384-131k.

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next AD384, reasoning_effort=xhigh sent PER-REQUEST via chat_template_kwargs (verified 2026-09-23: request overrides the unit's low pin; template supports low/medium/xhigh only, no off). Effort sweep variant of flashnext-ad384-131k.

deepswe2 at MEDIUM. Daily Swift-Qwen3.8-27B Q5_K_M, MTP n=2, 128K ctx, q4_0 KV, both 3060s (-ts 12,11). reasoning_effort=medium per-request overrides the unit pin; the Qwen3.8 template accepts low|medium|xhigh. xhigh was tried first (2026-10-01) and abandoned: 26k tokens on a task that still failed, plus two 40-minute client timeouts.

deepswe2 at MEDIUM. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next AD384 IQ4_XS on ONE 3060 (expert FFN on CPU; a 2-card split measured worse at every matched config), ctx 65536 (cut from 98304 for the 12GB card). Per-request effort overrides the unit's server-side low pin.

deepswe2 run. ISTA-DASLab Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Coder IQ1_M on the Strata CUDA engine: 256 of 512 experts kept (the code/tool/vision ones), 3.5-bit storage, arena 23.4 GB (vs the base IQ3_XXS's 42.9) so it sits in 61 GB RAM with room to spare. reasoning_effort=high is Strata's ceiling; the per-request value overrides the unit's shared setting. NOT speed-comparable to the llama.cpp lanes (Vulkan vs CUDA) - capability only.
